summary: ReactiveUI 25.0.1 reactive MVVM, commands, activation, routing, lean and System.Reactive-compatible packages, and binding migration guidance.
recommendedPatterns: Use ReactiveObject and ReactiveCommand for mutable state and user actions.
Prefer WhenAnyValue and OAPH/source-generator derived properties over imperative setter side effects.
Use the ReactiveUI.Binding generator for supported static binding paths; address every RXUIBIND diagnostic before running the application.
Plan upgrades from legacy ReactiveUI codebases by modernizing startup, disposal, command handling, and generator usage incrementally.
avoidPatterns: Do not create long-lived subscriptions in constructors without disposal.
Do not mutate UI-bound state from background threads.
Do not combine the lean ReactiveUI and ReactiveUI.Reactive package families in one application.
Do not leave legacy initialization, obsolete collection types, or stale package combinations in upgraded apps when a modern equivalent exists.
setupSteps: Select the correct platform package for the target UI stack.
Align ReactiveUI 25.0.1 core and platform packages with ReactiveUI.Binding 8.6.0 and ReactiveUI.Primitives 8.2.0.
For legacy upgrades, align packages first, then replace obsolete patterns incrementally with modern ReactiveUI guidance.
commonPitfalls: Mixing imperative state mutation with derived observable state.
Failing to scope bindings with activation on XAML-style platforms during upgrades.
Ignoring RXUIBIND diagnostics: unsupported generated binding call sites can throw at runtime.
Assuming reflection-based ViewModel discovery in WhenActivated is trim-safe.

features: ReactiveUI.Binding static binding generation and RXUIBIND diagnostics
options: WPF, WinForms, WinUI, MAUI, Blazor, AndroidX, Avalonia, or Uno host package
Core routing or DynamicData-based ReactiveUI.Routing extensions
App-wide main-thread/task-pool sequencers and service registrations
packageSelection: ReactiveUI 25.0.1: default to ReactiveUI with the matching lean platform package; ReactiveUI.Binding 8.6.0 and ReactiveUI.Primitives 8.2.0 are its binding and reactive foundations.
Full System.Reactive compatibility: choose ReactiveUI.Reactive plus matching *.Reactive platform packages instead of the lean family, never both.
Add ReactiveUI.Routing or ReactiveUI.Routing.Reactive only for DynamicData change-set routing/auto-persist helpers.
Add ReactiveUI.Testing 25.0.1 only to test projects; use TUnit for new tests.
sourceGeneratorGuidance: Use ReactiveUI.SourceGenerators 4.2.0 for properties, OAPHs, commands, IViewFor, IReactiveObject, collections, and supported hosts.
Use ReactiveUI.Binding 8.6.0's included generator for supported static WhenAnyValue, Bind, OneWayBind, BindCommand, and ToProperty call sites; fix all RXUIBIND diagnostics.
Use manual core APIs only for dynamic or unsupported generator scenarios and document the limitation.
compatibilityNotes: ReactiveUI 25.0.1 lean and .Reactive distributions share the same MVVM shape but expose different reactive interop types; select exactly one flavor.
Lean uses RxVoid/ISequencer/Signal; .Reactive uses Unit/IScheduler/Subject for existing Rx boundaries.
Core targets net8.0 through net11.0 and net462/net472/net481; Android, Apple, and MAUI targets require net10.0 or newer in the 25.0.1 source matrix.
As of 25.0.1, IInteraction<TInput,TOutput>.Handle(input) returns IObservable<TOutput> again; Interaction<TInput,TOutput>.WhenHandled(input) also returns IObservable<TOutput>.
Binding types such as IViewFor and Interaction now live in ReactiveUI.Binding (or ReactiveUI.Binding.Reactive); ReactiveUI supplies the global using.
Core routing remains in ReactiveUI; DynamicData-based routing extensions moved to ReactiveUI.Routing.
migrationGuidance: Move Fody and handwritten boilerplate to ReactiveUI.SourceGenerators before broad behavioral refactoring.
Build after upgrading binding packages and resolve RXUIBIND diagnostics; private or nested controls used by generated bindings may need internal visibility or an Unsafe overload.

For trimming, pass an explicit ViewModel observable to WhenActivated rather than relying on reflection-based lookup; review hand-written IReactiveObject PropertyChanged and binding write-thread behavior.
Prefer lean ReactiveUI/ReactiveUI.Primitives for new code; use the .Reactive family only when existing public API compatibility requires it.
Move constructor-created view subscriptions into WhenActivated and preserve interaction, command exception, and scheduler behavior with tests.
